key_insight: Magnesium alloy joints are difficult to weld reliably, so the review emphasizes process choice and parameter control to reduce cracking and preserve joint integrity.
engineering_relevance: The paper is relevant to lightweight automotive and advanced structural design because it compares weldability, defect risks, and joint performance across major Mg welding routes.
method: Reviewed scientific databases and patents using targeted keywords
Compared fusion, friction, diffusion, explosive, and hybrid welding methods for Mg alloys
Highlighted key processes for AZ-series alloys, including GTAW, GMAW, LBW, and FSW
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes published studies and patent evidence, focusing on observed microstructure, mechanical behavior, and weld defects rather than new experimental trials.
watch_item: Magnesium welding remains highly sensitive to cracking and process variability, so results may not transfer directly across alloys, joint types, or heat-input conditions.
paper_title: Welding Techniques for Magnesium Alloy Joints: A Comprehensive Review
